title: Metric Lipschitz lexicographic bandits with known objective-tradeoff upper bounds
summary: The learner faces multiple reward objectives ordered by priority. Each round selects one arm and observes its complete reward vector. The comparator is the lexicographically optimal arm. Known tradeoff coefficients control improvements in lower-priority objectives relative to losses in higher-priority ones; performance is retained as signed regret for each objective.

model.instance: The action set is a public metric space $(\mathcal X,D)$ of diameter at most $1$, possibly with infinitely many arms; the required covering and activation interfaces are available. Each arm has $m$ fixed mean rewards $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m$, ordered by priority, and every mean function is $1$-Lipschitz. Each objective has oscillation at most $1$; irrelevant common additive shifts are unrestricted. A lexicographically optimal arm $x^\star$ exists. Ties are allowed at each priority; subsequent objectives are compared among arms optimal for all higher-priority objectives. The tradeoff coefficient is finite: $$\lambda_\star=\inf\!\left\{\lambda\ge0:\ \mu_i(x)-\mu_i(x^\star)\le\lambda\max_{j<i}\bigl(\mu_j(x^\star)-\mu_j(x)\bigr),\ \forall x\in\mathcal X,\ 2\le i\le m\right\}<\infty.$$ $$N_c(r)=\min\!\left\{n:\ \mathcal X\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{n}B_D(x_j,r),\ x_j\in\mathcal X\right\}.$$ Here $N_c(r)$ is the covering number at radius $r$. The objective-specific zooming quantities $N_z^{(i)}(r)$ use the source definitions on the corresponding near-optimal regions and cannot be replaced by the ambient dimension $d$.

operations.query_signature: Choose an arm $x_t$, then observe all $m$ reward coordinates of that arm. Conditional on past observations and the current arm, each coordinate is $1$-sub-Gaussian around its fixed mean; coordinates need not be independent. $$\mathbb E\!\left[e^{s(Y_{t,i}-\mu_i(x_t))}\mid\mathcal H_{t-1},x_t\right]\le e^{s^2/2}\qquad(s\in\mathbb R,\ 1\le i\le m).$$ Causal policies may use the public covering and activation interfaces. The metric space, $m,T,\delta_{\mathrm{conf}}$, and $\lambda\ge\lambda_\star$ are public. The mean functions and lexicographically optimal arm $x^\star$ are hidden. Observed feedback may be stored and reused computationally; unrevealed past information and additional queries to exhausted samples are unavailable. Any within-round full-function or common-sample two-point access must be explicitly specified.

model.instance: The public arm space is $\mathcal X=\{a\}\cup S$, where S is nonempty compact, $D(a,z)=1$ for every z in S, and $\operatorname{diam}(S)\le1/4$. There are exactly two fixed mean functions $\mu^1,\mu^2$, each 1-Lipschitz in D and each with oscillation at most one. Common additive offsets may differ between the two coordinates and are unrestricted; the gaps, local tradeoff, and regret are invariant under these offsets. The primary optimum set is $\mathcal X_1^*=\operatorname{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\mu^1(x)$, and a lexicographic optimum $x^*\in\operatorname{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X_1^*}\mu^2(x)$ exists. Primary ties are permitted. The finite local tradeoff is $\lambda_*=\inf\{b\ge0:\mu^2(x)-\mu^2(x^*)\le b[\mu^1(x^*)-\mu^1(x)]\ \forall x\in\mathcal X\}$. A finite upper bound $\lambda\ge\lambda_*\ge0$ is supplied to the policy.

operations.query_signature: At round t, choose one arm $X_t\in\mathcal X$ using past observations and independent internal randomness, then receive both coordinates $(Y_t^1,Y_t^2)$. Conditional on the past and current arm, $\mathbb E[\exp(\theta(Y_t^i-\mu^i(X_t)))\mid\mathcal H_{t-1},X_t]\le\exp(\theta^2/2)$ for all real theta and i=1,2. Cross-coordinate independence is not required. No unselected-arm feedback, same-round second pull, or historical requery is provided. Public inputs are T, the fact m=2, the compact metric and its anchor-plus-tie geometry, and the finite supplied upper bound lambda. No external confidence parameter is required by this expected-regret view. Mean functions, the primary-optimal arm set, and the lexicographic optimum are hidden. A measurable maximal-net oracle is available: given a nonempty compact subset U of the public metric space and a radius r>0, it returns a finite inclusion-maximal r-separated subset of U. Such a set covers U by closed radius-r balls. This geometric computation does not supply reward information and is not charged as an arm pull.

symbols.meaning: Signed cumulative regret for objective $i$
symbols.definition: The criterion is $R_i(T)=T\mu_i(x^\star)-\sum_t\mu_i(x_t)$; do not take positive parts or replace it with a scalarized objective.

symbols.meaning: Error-amplification factor induced by the known tradeoff coefficient
symbols.definition: $\Lambda_i(\lambda)=\sum_{j=0}^{i-1}\lambda^j$, with every zeroth power interpreted as one.

symbols.meaning: Target and summation index
symbols.definition: $i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$. Use $1\le j<i$ in the tradeoff expression and $0\le j<i$ in the geometric series.

symbols.meaning: Test parameter in the conditional sub-Gaussian moment-generating-function bound
symbols.definition: A conditional moment-generating-function inequality for every s defines observation noise. Here s is not a budget.

symbols.meaning: Covering radius and truncation radius in the multiscale decomposition
symbols.definition: These are auxiliary scales in algorithms or bounds, not environment dimension or rank.

symbols.meaning: Closed metric ball
symbols.definition: $B_D(x,r)=\{y\in\mathcal X:D(x,y)\le r\}$.

symbols.meaning: Minimum number of radius-$r$ balls needed to cover the action space
symbols.definition: The quantity is $N_c(r)=\min\{n:\mathcal X\subseteq\cup_{j=1}^nB_D(x_j,r),\ x_j\in\mathcal X\}$; it must be finite when invoking the covering algorithm.

symbols.meaning: The scaled near-optimal gap level for objective i.
symbols.definition: $\{x:\Lambda_i(\lambda)r/2<\mu_i(x^\star)-\mu_i(x)\le\Lambda_i(\lambda)r\}$.

symbols.meaning: Local covering number at a scaled gap level
symbols.definition: This is the minimum number of metric balls of radius $r/96$ needed to cover $\mathcal X^{(i)}(r)$. It is an analytical quantity and is not supplied to the algorithm.

symbols.meaning: The confidence parameter of the fixed-covering method.

symbols.meaning: The confidence parameter of the adaptive scaling algorithm.
